newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, Eurodollars end steady, await PPI.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, Eurodollars end steady, await PPI.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Eurodollar futures ended little changed on Friday as weekend inertia and anticipation of U.S. wholesale inflation and retail sales data, due at 1230 GMT, dampened activity.

March Euroyen finished unchanged against its CME close at 99.32 while June ended at 99.18 against 99.19. Turnover on the June contract overtook March for the second day, prompting expectations it would become the lead month next week.
"People are just rolling down the curve because there's no value left in March," said a trader with a European house.
"The market's very much factored in steady rates well into next year but I think they're underestimating the risk."
He said March Euroyen showed potential to rise to 99.42/44 but said activity had slowed significantly ahead of Japan's general election on October 20.
"The market is well underpinned so there's no reason to sell right now and as soon as it even leans to the downside, people are in buying it," he added.
Japanese government bond futures settled at 123.37 against their opening 123.43.
Eurodollar futures finished steady after shrugging off an unexpected decline in U.S. weekly jobless claims which caused a sell-off on U.S. treasuries overnight.
"You have to be careful with initial jobless claims because that number could easily reverse itself ahead of the non-farm payrolls in three weeks," said the dealer.
He said March Eurodollars looked supported at 94.17. They ended unchanged against their IMM close at 94.20. December were also steady at 94.31.
